name: Daguerreotype photography and public disclosure
description: A photographic process producing a detailed unique image on a silver-plated copper surface, developed by Daguerre after a partnership with Niépce.

date.label: 7 January 1839
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: Members of the French Académie des Sciences saw Daguerre’s pictures.
events.caveats: Showing pictures did not yet disclose the process publicly.

evidence.supports: Museum dates the presentation of pictures to January 7, 1839.

date.label: 19 August 1839
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: The process was explained before a joint session of the French academies after arrangements for state acquisition of rights.
events.caveats: The museum says Daguerre retained a patent on equipment; public disclosure did not mean zero equipment cost or unrestricted rights in every jurisdiction.

contributions.resource: A lifetime pension compensated Daguerre in exchange for process rights.

evidence.supports: The account describes the pension exchanged for rights.
The museum dates the session and describes a pension exchanged for rights.
The museum says the French government placed the process in the public domain.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest cited dated event for this scoped record; a surviving witness or publication is not itself the invention date.

caveats: Daguerreotype was not the beginning of photography: Niépce had earlier results; exposure times and portraiture practice later changed.

research.note: Second reader checked the Metropolitan Museum account for dates of showing and public disclosure, and retained the equipment patent and access qualification.

impact.note: The museum describes dissemination across countries and subsequent technical improvements to the process.

tier_reason: Provisional judgment of sourced consequences, following docs/importance.md; independent review required.
